messages:
alex: Quick sweep following last night's PG/kv timeout postmortem. We need: remediation owners, short timelines (<=2 wks where possible), runbook edits for triage commands, and a note on recurring patterns. I'll kick off a lightweight checklist.

pm_renee: thanks alex — can you paste the postmortem link and any hot fixes applied?

sre_bot: Incident report created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2026/pg-kv-timeout-1763449000 (summary attached). Auto-captured deploys + alert timeline.

alex: hot fix = rolled back canary routing to model-v2, forced failover of primary pg node. Details in doc. Immediate action: runbook needs clearer first-step checks for replication lag and circuit-breaker state.

maria: assigning myself to runbook edits for the DB triage section. I'll add explicit commands and quick thresholds. ETA 4 business days.

jonathan: i'll take ownership of the alert -> escalation path changes (pager play). Will add a step to check exporter metrics before escalating to oncall. ETA 3 business days.

alex: maria + jonathan thanks. devops do you want to own the 'automatic fallback' policy tweak to avoid noisy failovers?

devops: i'll own the fallback policy change and will prototype rate-limit window for the routing controller. ETA 1 week.

maria: draft for DB triage section (short form):
```
1) Check replication lag: `SELECT now() - pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp()`
   - if >30s -> escalate to infra and promote standby if needed
2) Check connections: `psql -c "select count(*) from pg_stat_activity;"`
3) Check wal sender/receiver status and disk IO `iostat -x`
4) If circuit-breaker tripped, run: `curl -X POST https://rb.internal/api/cb/reset -d '{"service":"pg"}'`
```
I'll add thresholds and links to dashboards.

jonathan: for pager path: add a pre-escalation step to DM oncall for 5m, include a quick dump command: `kubectl logs -l app=pg -n infra --tail=200` and `redis-cli info replication` for kv checks.

alex: good. Also note recurring pattern: similar partial timeouts seen 3x in last 9 weeks (tags: high write burst, bulk reindex jobs). We should add a runbook section 'when to throttle background jobs' and a recommended `pg_ctl`/`pgtune` checklist.

pm_renee: can someone own investigating bulk job scheduling policy? Owner + ETA please.

maria: i'll take initial triage of job scheduling interactions (where jobs spike write pressure). ETA 1 week for findings + recommended throttle defaults.

devops: will add a safe default throttle/limiter in the routing controller config and expose a feature flag. ETA 2 weeks including test.

alex: to keep follow-ups tracked: I'll create a short GH issue per action and link to the postmortem. Please include the runbook PRs as dependencies. If owners could add the issue numbers here when created that helps.

jonathan: created ISSUE-1298 for escalation path changes -> PR #412 pending.

maria: created ISSUE-1299 for DB triage edits -> PR #415 in draft.

devops: created ISSUE-1301 for fallback limiter -> working branch, will open PR next week.

pm_renee: fantastic. Let's do a quick cadence: owners ping in this thread with progress every 3 working days until PR merged. I'll mark the postmortem as 'followups scheduled' once all PRs are linked.

alex: one more: add a short 'playback' step in runbook to run through a dry triage (5-10min checklist) during oncall handoff to keep folks practiced. owner?

jonathan: i'll add the playback checklist into the pager docs.

sre_bot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up check-in in 3 days (1763713589).

alex: perfect. thanks everyone :thumbsup: let's keep items scoped small so we can close within 2 weeks for the critical ones.

maria: noted — I'll open PR for runbook edits by EOD Friday and tag reviewers.

devops: will share config diff for limiter in draft branch tomorrow.

jonathan: will finish pager edits and link ISSUE-1298 to postmortem by EOD.

pm_renee: logging this thread in the postmortem root so we have traceability. happy to help unblock.

alex: closing the loop here — next check-in in 3 days. If anything blocks earlier, ping me directly.
